2670ae0e44b3c5332dd99fa4713d822af9354126.summary: Group-IB report on BlackCat (also known as ALPHV), a Rust-based ransomware-as-a-service operation active from late 2021. It covers double and triple extortion, affiliate intrusion techniques, notable attacks on Change Healthcare, MGM Resorts, Caesars and others, the March 2024 exit scam, and the Cicada3301 successor. Several links to other groups are hedged.

hedges: Cybersecurity analysts suspect Cicada3301 is BlackCat 2.0 operating under a new name.
It is difficult to say for sure whether Cicada3301 fully adopted the ALPHV/BlackCat codebase; partial reuse seems more plausible.
Group-IB investigators find the overlap of two ransomware groups in the Estée Lauder incident unusual and possibly coincidental.
Caesars intruders were believed to be the same BlackCat/Scattered Spider team, as stated in an SEC filing.
BlackCat and Conti were said to have been behind the February 2022 attacks on European oil companies.
Some believe the Cicada3301 group may be a rebrand of BlackCat.
The catalyst for the BlackCat shutdown appears to have been greed; law enforcement may have contributed to pressure.
Given the heat on BlackCat, the Cicada3301 targeting of smaller businesses could be an attempt to stay under law enforcement's radar.

26c4e95ac89f39a362a2943a3c46440105edc9ff.summary: FBI-focused report (7 May 2024, The Record) on Scattered Spider, a hacking group that uses social engineering to get past multifactor authentication, then deploys ransomware or steals data for extortion. It cites attacks on MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment. FBI official Brett Leatherman urges victims to report quickly and says dismantling such groups is hard. A 19-year-old was arrested in January over $800,000 in cryptocurrency theft.
